rationale:
Evidence: iteration 1 (kp 2.5, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.6) still went off track on all 60 trials. Progress rose a little (oval 0.15, s-bend 0.16, slalom 0.11), but s-bend and slalom still show about 2 line-loss events and max_error about 0.062 to 0.063 m, just over the 0.06 m off-track limit. Lowering the gain did not fix the failure, so the gains are not the main problem.

Diagnosis: the sensors only span x = -0.02 to +0.02 m, and sensor_size is 0.008 m. The tape is 0.025 m wide, so its edge sits at 0.0125 m. Once the robot drifts about 0.02 m, the outer sensors see no tape, the summed reading drops below 0.05, and the line is lost. The line-loss response then has to recover from a blind state, and the robot leaves the track. Narrow sensor coverage is the likeliest cause, consistent with the Evaluator's note that geometry may be the limit.

Changes: (1) widen the sensor array to x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 so that the outer sensors still see tape at about 0.03 to 0.04 m offset, and (2) raise sensor_size to 0.012 m so each footprint covers more of the tape edge. Weights stay at -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1. Because the signal is a weighted average of sensor positions, doubling the spacing halves the signal per metre of offset. To keep turn response near the previous level (about 125 per m before, about 87 per m now), kp goes from 2.5 to 3.5. kd stays at 0.3 to damp the faster response. base_speed stays at 1.6 and line_loss stays last_direction, so the geometry change is the main variable.

Expected result: line_loss_events fall toward 0 or 1, max_error stays clear of 0.06 m, and progress rises above 0.2 on the s-bend and slalom. Hypotheses to check: (H1) line_loss_events drop when the outer sensors reach further; (H2) if runs still leave the track with line loss near 2, the line-loss response (search_left or search_right) is the next lever; (H3) if steering_oscillation rises above about 0.15, the wider array has made steering too sharp, so lower kp toward 2.5.
